label: fig:apertura
caption: Responses to a perturbation. Without corrections, the tilt in Śīrṣāsana tends to grow. In Śavāsana the relaxed arm falls back towards the floor.
alt: Responses to a perturbation. Without corrections, the tilt in Śīrṣāsana tends to grow. In Śavāsana the relaxed arm falls back towards the floor.

label: fig:tornare
caption: A ball and an arm at four moments. The grey ball in the third drawing marks the initial height. The bounce of the arm is schematic.
alt: A ball and an arm at four moments. The grey ball in the third drawing marks the initial height. The bounce of the arm is schematic.

label: fig:onda
caption: Displacement from the point of rest in a damped oscillator. The plot describes the ball’s return. For the arm, it illustrates the dying away of the motion, which is bounded by the floor.

label: fig:paesaggio
caption: Three potential energy profiles. The arrows on the slopes show the initial direction of motion after displacement from rest. On the flat section there is no restoring force towards any particular point.
alt: Three potential energy profiles. The arrows on the slopes show the initial direction of motion after displacement from rest. On the flat section there is no restoring force towards any particular point.

label: fig:basi
caption: Centre of mass and base of support in four asanas. The ochre strip shows the base in cross-section. For static equilibrium with support from the floor alone, the vertical line through the centre of mass must fall within the base. Whether an already moving body can recover also depends on its motion and control.
alt: Centre of mass and base of support in four asanas. The ochre strip shows the base in cross-section. For static equilibrium with support from the floor alone, the vertical line through the centre of mass must fall within the base. Whether an already moving body can recover also depends on its motion and control.

label: fig:sugiu
caption: A displacement raises the centre of mass of a suspended object and lowers that of an object pivoted below its centre of mass. The open circle marks the starting position.
alt: A displacement raises the centre of mass of a suspended object and lowers that of an object pivoted below its centre of mass. The open circle marks the starting position.

label: fig:paesaggiocorpo
caption: Schematic landscapes for the return of the arm in Śavāsana and the tilt of the uncorrected inverted pendulum associated with Śīrṣāsana.
alt: Schematic landscapes for the return of the arm in Śavāsana and the tilt of the uncorrected inverted pendulum associated with Śīrṣāsana.

label: fig:concacupola
caption: With two directions of displacement the landscape becomes a surface. Red marks the equilibrium, grey the displaced ball and blue its path.
alt: With two directions of displacement the landscape becomes a surface. Red marks the equilibrium, grey the displaced ball and blue its path.

label: fig:quote
caption: Five successive climbs of a ball in a bowl with friction, alternating from side to side. Each climb ends lower than the last.
alt: Five successive climbs of a ball in a bowl with friction, alternating from side to side. Each climb ends lower than the last.

label: fig:bilancio
caption: The ball’s energy balance at four moments. Potential energy is associated with height and kinetic energy with motion.
alt: The ball’s energy balance at four moments. Potential energy is associated with height and kinetic energy with motion.

label: fig:gradini
caption: Position and total energy of the damped oscillator. Energy never increases, and the slope vanishes at each turning point.
alt: Position and total energy of the damped oscillator. Energy never increases, and the slope vanishes at each turning point.

label: fig:escursionista
caption: A downhill path and its elevation. Green contours connect points at the same height. The path approaches the valley floor at 1,000 metres.

label: fig:braccio
caption: The arm falls back in Śavāsana, with its energy balance shown at each stage. The sum of the first two bars gives the altimeter, which never increases.
alt: The arm falls back in Śavāsana, with its energy balance shown at each stage. The sum of the first two bars gives the altimeter, which never increases.

label: fig:duegrafici
caption: Displacement of the ball from the bottom. With friction, oscillations die out. Without friction, their amplitude stays constant.
alt: Displacement of the ball from the bottom. With friction, oscillations die out. Without friction, their amplitude stays constant.

label: fig:patto
caption: Tolerance and initial displacement for a ball released from rest. For each tolerance <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, we seek a bound <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> on the initial displacement. Distances are measured from the bottom.
alt: Tolerance and initial displacement for a ball released from rest. For each tolerance ε, we seek a bound δ on the initial displacement. Distances are measured from the bottom.

label: fig:cratere
caption: A bowl with a rim. The surface at left shows the dashed rim and the path of a ball that stays inside. At right is a cross-section of the same bowl.

label: fig:uhp
caption: Utthita Hasta Pādāṅguṣṭhāsana and a synthetic centre-of-pressure trace seen from above. The circles and path are illustrative. A finite recording of this quantity alone cannot establish stability of the full state.
alt: Utthita Hasta Pādāṅguṣṭhāsana and a synthetic centre-of-pressure trace seen from above. The circles and path are illustrative. A finite recording of this quantity alone cannot establish stability of the full state.

label: fig:collepalline
caption: The exponentially growing mode near the summit. The displacement doubles at equal time intervals. The drawing exaggerates the motion so it is visible.
alt: The exponentially growing mode near the summit. The displacement doubles at equal time intervals. The drawing exaggerates the motion so it is visible.

label: fig:pendolonudo
caption: Śīrṣāsana and its simplest model, the inverted pendulum, with a rod pivoted at the base and a mass at the top.
alt: Śīrṣāsana and its simplest model, the inverted pendulum, with a rod pivoted at the base and a mass at the top.

label: fig:ventaglio
caption: A simple inverted pendulum 0.8 metres long, initially at rest one degree from vertical. The rounded angles are calculated from the linear model at intervals of 0.2 seconds.
alt: A simple inverted pendulum 0.8 metres long, initially at rest one degree from vertical. The rounded angles are calculated from the linear model at intervals of 0.2 seconds.

label: fig:raddoppio
caption: Growth of the tilt in the linear model, starting from rest. The doubling rate approaches that of the growing exponential mode.
alt: Growth of the tilt in the linear model, starting from rest. The doubling rate approaches that of the growing exponential mode.

label: fig:bastone
caption: A stick balanced on the palm at three moments. The dashed line drops vertically from the top of the stick. The ochre arrow shows how the hand moves.
alt: A stick balanced on the palm at three moments. The dashed line drops vertically from the top of the stick. The ochre arrow shows how the hand moves.

label: fig:lungocorto
caption: A longer rod tilts more slowly in this model, leaving more time to correct it.
alt: A longer rod tilts more slowly in this model, leaving more time to correct it.

label: fig:pendolo
caption: Śīrṣāsana with correction. Weight tends to increase the tilt, denoted by the Greek letter <math display="inline" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> (theta). The correction at the base tends to reduce it.
alt: Śīrṣāsana with correction. Weight tends to increase the tilt, denoted by the Greek letter θ (theta). The correction at the base tends to reduce it.

label: fig:somma
caption: Adding the gravitational potential and the correction term. Sufficient restoring action produces a minimum. With a weaker correction the maximum remains. The diagram assumes there is no delay.
alt: Adding the gravitational potential and the correction term. Sufficient restoring action produces a minimum. With a weaker correction the maximum remains. The diagram assumes there is no delay.

label: fig:corretto
caption: The effective potential with correction is green, and the original unstable potential is grey. The blue path shows a damped return in two position coordinates. Height represents potential energy alone, which can increase during the oscillations.
alt: The effective potential with correction is green, and the original unstable potential is grey. The blue path shows a damped return in two position coordinates. Height represents potential energy alone, which can increase during the oscillations.

label: fig:anello
caption: The feedback loop that sustains Śīrṣāsana.
alt: The feedback loop that sustains Śīrṣāsana.

label: fig:ritardo
caption: Four responses of the inverted pendulum with delayed control. The red line shows an illustrative amplitude threshold. The cross marks the first crossing. The equation, parameters and initial history are given in the model notes.

label: fig:dueconche
caption: Two wells and a rise. The ochre arrow marks the push. The dashed path follows a weak push and the solid path a stronger one.

caption: Four stages of the dropback and their schematic representation on a double-well landscape. The rise marks the transition between asanas.
alt: Four stages of the dropback and their schematic representation on a double-well landscape. The rise marks the transition between asanas.

label: fig:dropbacktre
caption: A double-well potential associated with the two asanas. The open circle marks the pass and the dashed line the ridge. The blue trajectory crosses the rise and settles in the right-hand well. Height represents potential energy, which can rise even as total energy falls.

caption: The passage from the right-hand well to the left-hand one. The height difference in green is the potential barrier. The energy supplied must also cover losses along the way.
alt: The passage from the right-hand well to the left-hand one. The height difference in green is the potential barrier. The energy supplied must also cover losses along the way.

label: fig:velocita
caption: Two pendulums at the same position with different subsequent motions.
alt: Two pendulums at the same position with different subsequent motions.

alt: Levels of total energy and the trajectory of a damped oscillator. Height never increases along the blue path.
